transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I've been feeling deeply depressed and sad, and it just doesn't seem to go away. It feels like this heavy emptiness has been with me every day for about ten months now. I just feel completely worn out.
Have you had these symptoms continuously for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two years, or is it a more recent development?
No, it hasn't been going on for two years. It actually started about ten months ago, but it has felt continuous and pretty much every day since then.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. I've completely lost interest in the hobbies and activities I used to love, and I just can't seem to find any pleasure or happiness in them anymore. Everything I used to enjoy just feels completely flat and empty now.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently?
No, I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or my weight. Everything seems to have stayed pretty much the same in that regard.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, or are you sleeping more than usual?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep patterns. It seems to be relatively normal, and I'm not having much trouble sleeping or sleeping more than usual.
Have you been feeling tired or fatigued almost every day, even when you've rested enough?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling unusually tired or fatigued. My physical energy levels seem to be pretty normal, even with everything else I've been feeling.
Have you been feeling excessive guilt, worthlessness, or self-criticism, even when it doesn't seem justified?
No, I haven't really been feeling guilty or blaming myself. It is more that I just feel a deep, constant sadness and a sense of emptiness inside.
Have you had these symptoms continuously for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two years, or is it a more recent development?
No, it hasn't been going on for two years. It started about ten months ago, but it has felt constant and everyday since then.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was Persistent Depressive Disorder, which requires symptoms lasting for at least two years. The patient explicitly stated that symptoms began ten months ago and have been continuous since, which falls short of the two-year duration required for Persistent Depressive Disorder. Therefore, Persistent Depressive Disorder is no longer a valid candidate. However, the patient endorses depressed mood and anhedonia nearly every day for ten months, without significant changes in sleep, appetite, fatigue, or guilt. This pattern meets the duration and symptom criteria for Major Depressive Disorder (at least two weeks of depressed mood or anhedonia plus other symptoms), and no better-fitting diagnosis is supported by the current data. Thus, the current candidate is Major Depressive Disorder.
